newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia housing industry welcomes data.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia housing industry welcomes data.

text.p: The Real Estate Institute of Australia (REIA) on Thursday welcomed a rise in housing finance numbers in January, saying it was an excellent sign for the housing market.
"REIA is encouraged by the January growth in housing finance approvals," president Don Brindley said in a statement.
Figures released earlier showed finance commitments for owner-occupied housing rose five percent by volume to 42,408 dwellings in January from a December level of 40,393, seasonally-adjusted.
But Brindley said the higher unemployment rate was knocking many people out of the home ownership market.

"The existing rate of unemployment, plus the fact that even those in a job are very unsure of their future career prospects, puts home ownership out of the reach of many young families today," he said.
Australia's seasonally-adjusted unemployment rate was at 8.8 percent in February against 8.6 percent in January, according to figures also released earlier on Thursday.
Master Builders Australia said the rise in housing finance was another indicator that the housing recovery was starting to strengthen.

"Conditions for an improved housing market for the remainder of 1997 are now in place with housing affordability the best it has been for the past two decades," national director economics and housing Wilhelm Harnisch said in a statement.
